raw:
The user wants app UI strings in Traditional Chinese. They have:
- s1: submit button for a feedback form (sends content to the team)
- s2: button in settings page that writes/saves changes
- s3: status text after changes are saved

They want only a JSON object with keys s1, s2, s3, values are strings, no other text.

For Traditional Chinese UI:
- s1: "送出意見" or "送出" — since it goes to the team, "送出意見" is a good button label. Buttons should be concise. "送出" alone is also fine but "送出意見" is clearer.
- s2: "儲存變更" or "儲存設定" — writing changes to settings. "儲存變更" is standard.
- s3: status text after changes written: "變更已儲存" — status message.

Note: the distinction between "送出" (submitting feedback to team) and "儲存" (saving changes locally/persisting). In Traditional Chinese, 送出 for submission, 儲存 for saving changes.

s3: "變更已儲存" — good. Could also be "已儲存變更" or "設定已更新". "變更已儲存" is concise and natural.

Output only the JSON object. Use double quotes, proper JSON. Maybe with proper escaping—no need. Traditional Chinese characters.

The user said "只輸出一個 JSON 物件...不要其他文字" — so output exactly:

{
  "s1": "送出意見",
  "s2": "儲存變更",
  "s3": "變更已儲存"
}

Should I format it as multi-line JSON or single line? Either is fine; a common format is pretty-printed. Just output JSON, no markdown code fences? They said no other text — code fences might count as other text. Safer to output raw JSON without fences. I'll output the JSON object plain.</think>{
  "s1": "送出意見",
  "s2": "儲存變更",
  "s3": "變更已儲存"
}
